response: The CPU, or Central Processing Unit, is the main chip in a computer that executes all instructions — it handles calculations, logic, and controls every other component. Think of it as the brain of the machine, Sir.

A GPU, or Graphics Processing Unit, was originally designed to render graphics but is now also used for AI, machine learning, and scientific computing. It runs thousands of small tasks in parallel, which is why it's much faster than a CPU for those workloads.
RAM stands for Random Access Memory — it's the fast, temporary storage your computer uses to hold data it's currently working with. More RAM means you can run more programs at once without slowdowns.

prompt: what is the difference between RAM and storage?
response: RAM is fast but temporary — data is lost when you power off. Storage like an SSD or HDD is slower but permanent. RAM holds what you're actively using; storage holds everything else.

An SSD, Solid State Drive, stores data on flash memory chips with no moving parts. It's much faster than a traditional hard drive, which makes your system boot quickly and load files almost instantly.
An HDD, Hard Disk Drive, stores data on spinning magnetic disks. It's slower than an SSD but typically much cheaper per gigabyte, so it's still used for large storage needs.
The motherboard is the main circuit board that connects all components — CPU, RAM, GPU, storage, and ports. Everything in a PC communicates through it.
A PSU, Power Supply Unit, converts AC power from the wall into the DC voltages your components need. It powers everything in your PC.
Overclocking means running a CPU or GPU faster than its official rated speed to get more performance. It generates more heat and can reduce the chip's lifespan if done without proper cooling.
When a CPU or GPU gets too hot, it automatically slows itself down to prevent damage — that's thermal throttling. It's a safety mechanism built into modern processors.

An operating system, or OS, is the core software that manages all hardware and software on a computer. Windows, macOS, and Linux are the most common ones. It handles memory, processes, files, and user interfaces.
Linux is a free, open-source operating system kernel. It powers servers, Android phones, supercomputers, and embedded devices. Distributions like Ubuntu, Debian, and Arch Linux build on top of it.
Windows is Microsoft's operating system — the most widely used desktop OS in the world. It's known for broad software compatibility and ease of use.
macOS is Apple's operating system for Mac computers. It's built on a Unix foundation and is known for its clean design, tight hardware-software integration, and security.
The kernel is the core of an operating system. It sits between the hardware and software, managing CPU time, memory, and device communication. Everything else runs on top of it.
Open source means the source code is publicly available — anyone can read, modify, and distribute it. Linux, Python, and Firefox are well-known open-source projects.
A driver is software that lets the operating system communicate with a specific hardware device, like a graphics card or printer. Without the right driver, the hardware won't work properly.
A virtual machine, or VM, is software that simulates a complete computer inside your real computer. You can run a different OS in a window, isolated from your main system.
Docker is a platform for running applications in lightweight containers. A container packages the app and all its dependencies together, so it runs identically on any machine.
An API, Application Programming Interface, is a set of rules that lets two software systems talk to each other. When an app uses Google Maps or processes a payment, it's calling an API.
The internet is a global network of interconnected computers that communicate using standardized protocols. It carries email, web pages, video streams, and virtually all digital communication.
An IP address is a unique numerical label assigned to every device on a network, like an address for your house. IPv4 uses four numbers like 192.168.1.1, while IPv6 uses a longer hexadecimal format.
DNS, Domain Name System, translates human-readable domain names like google.com into IP addresses that computers can understand. It's essentially the phone book of the internet.

HTTP, HyperText Transfer Protocol, is the foundation of data communication on the web. When you visit a website, your browser sends HTTP requests and gets responses back. HTTPS is the encrypted version.
HTTPS is HTTP with encryption via TLS. It protects the data between your browser and the server so nobody can intercept or tamper with it. You'll see the padlock icon in your browser.
A router directs network traffic between devices and the internet. It assigns IP addresses to devices on your local network and routes data packets to the right destination.
Bandwidth is the maximum data transfer rate of a network connection, usually measured in megabits or gigabits per second. Higher bandwidth means more data can flow at once.
Latency is the delay between sending a request and getting a response — measured in milliseconds. Low latency is critical for gaming and real-time communication.

A VPN, Virtual Private Network, creates an encrypted tunnel between your device and a server, masking your real IP address and encrypting your traffic. It's used for privacy and to bypass geographic restrictions.
A firewall monitors and filters incoming and outgoing network traffic based on security rules. It acts as a barrier between trusted internal networks and untrusted external ones.

TCP, Transmission Control Protocol, ensures data is delivered reliably and in the correct order. It breaks data into packets, sends them, and confirms each one was received. Most web traffic uses TCP.

UDP, User Datagram Protocol, sends data without waiting for confirmation. It's faster than TCP but less reliable. It's used for video streaming, gaming, and voice calls where speed matters more than perfect delivery.

WiFi is wireless networking technology that lets devices connect to the internet without cables, using radio waves. Standards like WiFi 6 and WiFi 7 offer faster speeds and better handling of many connected devices.
Bluetooth is a short-range wireless technology for connecting devices like headphones, keyboards, and phones. It operates within about 10 meters and uses low power.

Artificial intelligence is the field of computer science focused on building systems that can perform tasks that normally require human intelligence — like recognizing speech, making decisions, or understanding language.
Machine learning is a branch of AI where systems learn patterns from data instead of being explicitly programmed. The more data they train on, the better they get at their task.
Deep learning is a type of machine learning that uses neural networks with many layers. It excels at image recognition, speech, and language tasks. It's behind most modern AI breakthroughs.
A neural network is a computational model inspired by the human brain. It consists of layers of interconnected nodes that process data, learn from examples, and make predictions.

prompt: what is a large language model?
response: A large language model, or LLM, is an AI trained on massive amounts of text to understand and generate human language. GPT-4, Claude, and Gemini are examples. They power most modern AI assistants.
ChatGPT is an AI assistant made by OpenAI, built on their GPT series of large language models. It can answer questions, write code, draft emails, and hold conversations.
Claude is an AI assistant made by Anthropic. It's designed to be helpful, harmless, and honest, and is known for handling complex reasoning and long documents well.

A transformer is the neural network architecture behind most modern AI language models. It uses a mechanism called attention to understand relationships between words across an entire text, not just sequentially.
Training data is the dataset used to teach a machine learning model. The quality and quantity of this data directly determines how well the model performs.
Overfitting happens when a model learns the training data too well, including its noise and quirks, and then performs poorly on new, unseen data. It memorized instead of learning.

A fine-tuned model starts from a pre-trained model and is further trained on a smaller, specific dataset to specialize its behavior — for example, training a general LLM to follow instructions or answer medical questions.
Ollama is an open-source tool that lets you run large language models locally on your own machine, without sending data to external servers. It supports models like Llama, Mistral, and Phi.
Cloud computing means using servers, storage, and software over the internet instead of on your own hardware. AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure are the biggest providers. You pay for what you use.
AWS, Amazon Web Services, is the world's largest cloud platform. It offers hundreds of services including virtual servers, databases, AI tools, and storage — used by companies of all sizes.
Microsoft Azure is a cloud computing platform offering infrastructure, AI services, DevOps tools, and more. It's deeply integrated with Microsoft's software ecosystem.
Google Cloud Platform is Google's cloud offering, known for its data analytics, AI capabilities, and Kubernetes container management. It runs on the same infrastructure as Google's own products.
Serverless means you run code without managing servers — the cloud provider handles all the infrastructure automatically. You're only charged when your code actually runs.
A CDN, Content Delivery Network, distributes your content across servers worldwide so users load it from the nearest location. This reduces latency and makes websites faster globally.
SaaS, Software as a Service, means software delivered over the internet rather than installed locally. Gmail, Spotify, and Notion are SaaS products — you access them through a browser.
Cybersecurity is the practice of protecting computers, networks, and data from unauthorized access, attacks, and damage. It covers everything from encryption to vulnerability patching.
Encryption converts data into an unreadable format using a key, so only authorized parties can decrypt and read it. AES and RSA are the most common encryption algorithms.
Instead of storing passwords as plain text, systems store a hash — a fixed-length fingerprint of the password. If the database is stolen, the attacker only gets hashes, not actual passwords.

Two-factor authentication, 2FA, requires a second proof of identity beyond your password — like a code from your phone. Even if someone steals your password, they can't log in without the second factor.
A DDoS, Distributed Denial of Service attack, floods a server with massive amounts of traffic from many machines at once, overwhelming it and making it unavailable to legitimate users.
SQL injection is an attack where malicious SQL code is inserted into a query through user input, potentially letting attackers read, modify, or delete database contents.
Phishing is a social engineering attack where attackers trick people into revealing credentials or clicking malicious links by impersonating a trusted source, usually via email.
A zero-day is a security flaw that's unknown to the software vendor, so there's no patch yet. Attackers who find one can exploit it before any defense is in place.

End-to-end encryption means only the sender and receiver can read the message — not even the service provider. WhatsApp and Signal use this. Your messages are encrypted on your device and decrypted only on the recipient's.
Python is a high-level, easy-to-read programming language used for web development, data science, AI, automation, and scripting. It's one of the most popular languages in the world.
JavaScript is the primary language of the web — it runs in browsers to make pages interactive. With Node.js it also runs on servers. Virtually every website uses it.
TypeScript is a superset of JavaScript that adds static type checking. It catches errors at compile time rather than runtime, making large codebases much easier to maintain.
Rust is a systems programming language focused on memory safety and performance, without a garbage collector. It's used for operating systems, game engines, and performance-critical software.
Go, or Golang, is a compiled language made by Google. It's known for simplicity, fast compilation, and excellent concurrency support. It's widely used for backend services and cloud tools.
C++ is a powerful, high-performance language used for game engines, operating systems, and embedded systems. It gives developers fine-grained control over memory but requires careful management.
A compiled language translates source code into machine code before execution. This makes it fast at runtime but requires a build step. C, C++, Go, and Rust are compiled languages.
An interpreted language runs code line by line without a prior compilation step. Python and JavaScript are interpreted, which makes them more flexible but typically slower than compiled languages.
Object-oriented programming, OOP, organizes code around objects — bundles of data and behavior. The main concepts are classes, inheritance, encapsulation, and polymorphism.

Functional programming treats computation as the evaluation of mathematical functions, avoids changing state, and emphasizes immutability. Haskell is purely functional; Python and JavaScript support functional styles.
Version control tracks changes to code over time, allowing teams to collaborate, revert mistakes, and maintain a history. Git is the dominant version control system today.
Git is a distributed version control system that tracks changes in code. Every developer has a full copy of the repository history. GitHub and GitLab are platforms built on top of Git.
GitHub is a cloud-based platform for hosting Git repositories. It adds collaboration features like pull requests, issues, and CI/CD workflows. Microsoft owns it.
An algorithm is a step-by-step set of instructions to solve a problem. Sorting a list, finding the shortest path, and searching a database all require specific algorithms.
A database is an organized collection of structured data, managed by a database management system. It lets you store, query, update, and delete data efficiently.
SQL, Structured Query Language, is the standard language for working with relational databases. You use it to create tables, insert data, and run queries to retrieve or modify records.
A relational database stores data in tables with rows and columns, and uses relationships between tables to organize data. PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQLite are popular examples.

NoSQL databases store data in flexible formats like documents, key-value pairs, or graphs instead of tables. MongoDB, Redis, and Cassandra are popular NoSQL databases, used when flexibility or scale is needed.
PostgreSQL is a powerful, open-source relational database known for its reliability, feature set, and standards compliance. It supports complex queries, JSON, and advanced data types.
MongoDB is a NoSQL document database that stores data as JSON-like documents. It's flexible and scales well horizontally, making it popular for web applications with rapidly changing data models.
Redis is an in-memory key-value store, extremely fast because it keeps all data in RAM. It's used for caching, sessions, real-time leaderboards, and pub/sub messaging.
React is a JavaScript library made by Meta for building user interfaces. It uses a component-based model where each piece of the UI is a reusable component that manages its own state.
Vue is a progressive JavaScript framework for building user interfaces. It's known for being approachable and easy to integrate incrementally into existing projects.
Node.js lets you run JavaScript on the server side. It's fast, non-blocking, and event-driven, making it well-suited for real-time applications and APIs.
Vite is a modern front-end build tool that provides an extremely fast development server using native ES modules. It's commonly used with React, Vue, and Svelte projects.
REST, Representational State Transfer, is an architectural style for APIs that uses standard HTTP methods — GET, POST, PUT, DELETE — to interact with resources identified by URLs.
GraphQL is an API query language that lets clients request exactly the data they need, nothing more and nothing less. It replaces REST for many applications where flexibility is important.
A cookie is a small piece of data stored in your browser by a website. It's used to remember sessions, preferences, and track user activity across visits.

prompt: what is a token in authentication?
response: An authentication token is a string that proves your identity after logging in. JWT, JSON Web Tokens, are the most common format — the server issues one and the client sends it with every request.
WebSocket is a protocol that enables full-duplex communication between a client and server over a single, persistent connection. It's used for real-time features like chat and live updates.
An app store is a digital marketplace for downloading and updating mobile applications. Apple's App Store and Google's Play Store are the two dominant platforms.
Android is Google's mobile operating system, powering the majority of smartphones worldwide. It's based on Linux and is open-source, used by manufacturers like Samsung, OnePlus, and many others.
iOS is Apple's mobile operating system for iPhone and iPad. It's known for its smooth performance, strong security, and tight integration with Apple's hardware and services.
A smartphone is a mobile phone with an advanced operating system that runs apps, browses the internet, handles email, and supports touch input. Modern ones also include powerful cameras and sensors.
5G is the fifth generation of mobile network technology. It offers dramatically faster speeds, lower latency, and the capacity to connect many more devices simultaneously compared to 4G.
An embedded system is a computer built into a device to perform a specific function — like the controller in a microwave, a car's engine management unit, or a smart thermostat.
IoT, the Internet of Things, refers to everyday devices connected to the internet — smart bulbs, thermostats, wearables, and industrial sensors that collect and exchange data.
A microcontroller is a compact integrated circuit with a CPU, RAM, and programmable I/O on a single chip. Arduino and ESP32 are popular platforms for hobbyist and IoT projects.

Moore's Law is the observation that the number of transistors on a chip roughly doubles every two years, leading to exponential growth in computing power. It has slowed in recent years as physical limits are approached.
A transistor is the fundamental building block of modern electronics — a tiny switch that controls electrical current. Modern processors contain billions of them packed onto a chip.
DevOps is a set of practices that combines software development and IT operations to shorten development cycles and deliver software more reliably. It emphasizes automation, CI/CD, and collaboration.

CI/CD stands for Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery. CI automatically tests code when changes are pushed; CD automatically deploys passing code to production. It speeds up and de-risks software releases.
Kubernetes is an open-source system for automating the deployment, scaling, and management of containerized applications. It orchestrates Docker containers across clusters of machines.

A microservice architecture breaks an application into small, independent services that each handle a specific function and communicate over APIs. It's easier to scale and update than a monolithic app.
Agile is a software development methodology that delivers work in short iterations called sprints, emphasizes collaboration, and adapts to changing requirements rather than following a rigid plan.

A blockchain is a distributed ledger where data is stored in blocks linked together cryptographically. It's transparent, tamper-resistant, and doesn't require a central authority. Bitcoin and Ethereum use it.
Cryptocurrency is digital currency secured by cryptography on a blockchain. Bitcoin was the first; Ethereum, Solana, and thousands of others followed. Transactions are decentralized, peer-to-peer.
A smart contract is self-executing code stored on a blockchain that automatically enforces the terms of an agreement when conditions are met, without needing an intermediary.
Web3 is a vision for a decentralized internet built on blockchain technology, where users own their data and digital assets rather than relying on centralized platforms.

Quantum computing uses quantum mechanical phenomena — superposition and entanglement — to perform certain computations exponentially faster than classical computers. It's still largely experimental but promising for cryptography and drug discovery.
A qubit is the basic unit of quantum information, analogous to a classical bit but it can exist in a superposition of both 0 and 1 simultaneously, enabling quantum parallelism.

Edge computing processes data closer to where it's generated — on devices or local servers — rather than sending everything to the cloud. It reduces latency and bandwidth usage for real-time applications.
Augmented reality overlays digital information onto the real world, usually through a camera or headset. Apple Vision Pro and Microsoft HoloLens are examples of AR hardware.
Virtual reality immerses you in a fully computer-generated environment using a headset. Meta Quest, PlayStation VR, and Valve Index are popular VR platforms.

A language model is an AI system trained to predict and generate text. Modern large language models like GPT-4 and Claude are trained on vast internet text and can converse, summarize, write code, and more.
Prompt engineering is the practice of crafting inputs to AI models to get the best possible outputs. The way you phrase a question significantly affects the quality and style of the AI's response.

RAG, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, combines a language model with a search system. Instead of relying on memorized knowledge, the model retrieves relevant documents and uses them to generate accurate, up-to-date answers.

A GPU cluster is a group of servers each equipped with multiple GPUs, connected with high-speed networking. Training large AI models requires thousands of GPUs running in parallel for weeks or months.
CUDA is NVIDIA's parallel computing platform that lets developers write programs that run on GPUs. It's the foundation of most deep learning frameworks like PyTorch and TensorFlow.
PyTorch is an open-source machine learning framework developed by Meta. It's the most popular library for training neural networks, known for its flexibility and Pythonic design.
TensorFlow is an open-source machine learning framework developed by Google. It's widely used for production AI systems and supports deployment across many platforms.

LoRA, Low-Rank Adaptation, is a technique for efficiently fine-tuning large language models by training only a small set of additional parameters rather than the full model. It dramatically reduces the compute and memory required.
Tokenization is the process of breaking text into tokens — words, subwords, or characters — that a language model can process numerically. Every model has a vocabulary of tokens it understands.

prompt: what is the difference between AI and automation?
response: Automation follows fixed rules to perform repetitive tasks — it doesn't learn. AI learns from data and can handle new, unseen situations. A conveyor belt is automation; a system that recognizes defects in products is AI.

NLP, Natural Language Processing, is the branch of AI that enables computers to understand, interpret, and generate human language. It powers search engines, chatbots, translation, and voice assistants.
Computer vision is the AI field that enables machines to interpret and understand visual information from images and video — used in self-driving cars, medical imaging, and facial recognition.
A self-driving car uses cameras, radar, LiDAR, and AI to navigate without human input. It perceives its environment, plans a route, and controls steering, throttle, and brakes autonomously.
LiDAR, Light Detection and Ranging, uses laser pulses to build precise 3D maps of the environment. It's a key sensor in autonomous vehicles and robotics.
A robot is a machine that can carry out complex actions automatically, often programmable and capable of sensing its environment. Modern robots combine mechanics, electronics, and AI software.

prompt: what is the difference between hardware and software?
response: Hardware is the physical components of a computer — the chips, screens, and cables you can touch. Software is the programs and operating systems that run on that hardware.
Binary is the base-2 number system computers use internally, representing all data as sequences of 0s and 1s. Every file, image, and instruction is ultimately stored as binary.

prompt: what is a bit and a byte?
response: A bit is the smallest unit of data — a single 0 or 1. A byte is 8 bits. A kilobyte is 1,024 bytes, a megabyte is 1,024 kilobytes, and so on up to terabytes and beyond.
A programming language is a formal set of instructions humans write to tell computers what to do. There are hundreds of them — each with different syntax, strengths, and use cases.

Debugging is the process of finding and fixing errors in code. It involves reproducing the problem, isolating the cause, and correcting it — one of the most time-consuming parts of software development.
A framework is a pre-built structure that provides tools, libraries, and conventions to speed up development. React is a frontend framework; Django is a backend one.
A library is a collection of pre-written code you can call in your program to perform common tasks — like making HTTP requests or parsing JSON — without writing everything from scratch.
A cache stores frequently accessed data in a fast-access location so future requests can be served faster. Browsers cache web pages, CPUs cache memory data, and applications cache database results.
A server is a computer or program that provides services or resources to other computers, called clients, over a network. Web servers, database servers, and file servers are common examples.

prompt: what is the difference between frontend and backend?
response: The frontend is everything the user sees and interacts with — the interface. The backend is the server-side logic, databases, and APIs that power it behind the scenes.
Responsive design means a website adapts its layout to different screen sizes — desktop, tablet, and mobile — using flexible grids and CSS media queries.

An IDE, Integrated Development Environment, is a software application that provides code editing, syntax highlighting, debugging, and build tools in one place. VS Code, JetBrains, and Xcode are popular IDEs.
Visual Studio Code is a free, open-source code editor made by Microsoft. It's the most popular editor for web development, supporting hundreds of extensions and built-in Git integration.
A package manager automates installing, updating, and removing software libraries. npm is for JavaScript, pip for Python, and apt for Debian-based Linux systems.
npm, Node Package Manager, is the package manager for JavaScript and Node.js. It hosts millions of open-source packages you can add to your projects with a single command.
A pull request is a way to propose changes to a codebase in Git. You push your changes to a branch, open a PR, and team members review it before merging it into the main branch.

Phi is a family of small but capable language models made by Microsoft. Phi-3.5-mini is notable for being highly efficient — it performs competitively with much larger models while running on consumer hardware.
Llama is a family of open-source large language models from Meta. Llama 3 and later versions are among the best open-weight models available, widely used for local AI deployments.
Mistral is a French AI company that produces highly efficient open-source language models. Mistral 7B and Mixtral are popular for their strong performance relative to their size.

prompt: what is a neural network layer?
response: A layer in a neural network is a set of neurons that processes input and passes its output to the next layer. Deep networks have many layers — each learns increasingly abstract features of the data.

Backpropagation is the algorithm used to train neural networks. It calculates how much each weight contributed to the prediction error and adjusts the weights to reduce that error over many iterations.

prompt: what is a GPU used for in AI?
response: GPUs massively accelerate AI training and inference by running thousands of matrix multiplication operations in parallel. Training a large model on a CPU would take years; on GPUs it takes days or weeks.
Inference is the process of using a trained AI model to make predictions on new data. Training is done once; inference happens every time someone uses the model.

Quantization reduces the precision of a model's weights — for example, from 32-bit floats to 4-bit integers. This makes models smaller and faster to run with minimal accuracy loss, enabling them to run on consumer hardware.

prompt: what is the difference between supervised and unsupervised learning?
response: Supervised learning trains on labeled data — the model learns from examples with correct answers. Unsupervised learning finds patterns in unlabeled data on its own, like clustering similar items together.

Reinforcement learning trains an AI agent by rewarding good actions and penalizing bad ones. The agent learns by trial and error to maximize cumulative reward. It's behind AlphaGo and many game-playing AIs.
A data center is a facility housing large numbers of servers, storage systems, and networking equipment. Cloud providers operate massive data centers around the world to deliver their services.

Latency is how long a single request takes to complete. Throughput is how many requests a system can handle per second. A fast API with low latency can still have limited throughput if it can't handle many parallel requests.
Een processor, ook wel CPU genoemd, is de kern van een computer. Hij voert alle berekeningen en instructies uit — hij stuurt het geheugen aan, verwerkt data en zorgt dat alles samenwerkt.
Kunstmatige intelligentie, of AI, is computertechnologie die menselijke taken nabootst zoals begrijpen, leren en beslissingen nemen. Denk aan spraakherkenning, vertaling, en AI-assistenten zoals ik.
Het internet is een wereldwijd netwerk van verbonden computers die communiceren via gestandaardiseerde protocollen. Het draagt e-mail, websites, video en vrijwel alle digitale communicatie.

Een database is een georganiseerde verzameling gegevens die je efficiënt kunt opslaan, opvragen en bewerken. SQL-databases zoals MySQL gebruiken tabellen; NoSQL-databases zoals MongoDB gebruiken flexibele documenten.
Cloud opslag betekent dat je bestanden op externe servers worden bewaard via het internet, in plaats van op je eigen apparaat. Google Drive, OneDrive en Dropbox zijn bekende voorbeelden.
Cybersecurity beschermt computers, netwerken en data tegen onbevoegde toegang, aanvallen en schade. Het omvat encryptie, firewalls, authenticatie en het patchen van kwetsbaarheden.
